note: Classes describe the kind of document a corpus case represents, so quality is measured per class instead of extrapolated from one synthetic sample to every DOCX or PDF. Signals are the minimum observable properties a document of the class must show in an inspect result; they identify mislabelled cases, they do not define quality.

classes.description: DOCX whose body is running text without headings, tables or figures.
DOCX with a heading hierarchy, lists and notes.
DOCX whose evidence depends on structural tables.
DOCX with more than one section, headers, footers or page-number fields.
DOCX carrying figures, shapes or comment anchors.
PDF with a text layer and no reconstructed tables or figures.
PDF whose headings and paragraphs are reconstructed from the text layer.
PDF whose evidence depends on inferred tables.
PDF carrying image XObjects or annotation overlays.
Input that is neither DOCX nor PDF and must be rejected before parsing.
Container whose package or object structure is broken and must be rejected with a typed error.
Document whose markup or syntax is invalid and must be rejected with a typed error.
Input that exceeds a published ingestion limit and must be rejected before parsing.
